al-andalus.note: No Andalusi style; Arabic traditional lists and Maghreb frequent names. Places mix Iberian and Maghreb towns.

aztec.note: Nahua given names; places are Mexican GeoNames places with a Nahuatl ending and no Spanish colonial prefix.

bagan.note: Burmese names are syllable compounds without a surname.

barbarian-norse.note: Viking generator has no town list; places are Scandinavian and Icelandic GeoNames places.

bastide.note: No Occitan style; Norman and Catalan lists plus frequent French names attested in historical lists.

budj-bim.note: Places reuse the Aboriginal name list (no Aboriginal gazetteer in Namebench).

chinese.note: No dated Chinese list in Namebench: frequent present-day names only, romanised (most Chinese-region forenames in the database are Han characters, so the Latin pool is small).

drow-enclave.note: Places use the elven city generator.

duergar-hold.note: Dwarf styles stand in for duergar.

egyptian-planned.note: Ancient Egyptian names with filiation (sa = son of, sat = daughter of); places are present-day Egyptian places.

ethiopian-highland.note: Ethiopian naming: the second name is the father's given name.

european-organic.note: Generic western Europe: medieval lists and attested frequent names.

great-zimbabwe.note: Shona traditional names; surnames are totem-clan style.

guarani-village.note: Paraguay pools; Guarani names are sparse in the database.

halfling.note: Places use the generic fantasy town generator.

hausa-kano.note: Hausa and Islamic traditional lists; frequent Nigerian names are mostly modern and are left out.

himalayan-terraces.note: Tibetan names; places are Nepali GeoNames places.

inca.note: Quechua-region frequent names are mostly Spanish; no Inca list in Namebench.

indian-temple.note: No Sanskrit style; Hindu traditional list and Hindi.

indus-planned.note: No Indus-era style; Sanskritic traditional list.

inuit-camp.note: Inuit list is a single flat list shared by all name pools; places are Greenland GeoNames places.

javanese-courts.note: Sanskritic traditional list plus Indonesian names; no Javanese style.

kraal.note: Traditional Zulu names; surnames are frequent Zulu and Xhosa clan names.

maori-pa.note: New Zealand pools filtered by Maori phonotactics (open syllables of h k m n p r t w ng wh).

maya.note: Maya names; places are Guatemalan and Belizean GeoNames places.

merfolk-tidal.note: Mermaid names mix mythological and ordinary names.

mesopotamian.note: Sumerian, Babylonian and Assyrian lists (mar = son of); places are present-day Iraqi places.

mississippian.note: Southeastern tribes of the Pan-Native-American list; no Mississippian style.

mongol-ordu.note: Mongolian pools (unisex: the database has almost no gendered Mongolian forenames).

myconid-colony.note: Mushroom species name parts; no myconid style.

native-iroquoian.note: Eastern Woodlands tribes of the Pan-Native-American list.

native-plains.note: Plains tribes of the Pan-Native-American list.

native-pueblo.note: Hopi, Zuni and Laguna entries of the Pan-Native-American list.

necropolis.note: Ancient Egyptian names stand in; no undead style.

newar.note: Nepali lists; Newar names are sparse in the database.

norse-ringfort.note: Viking generator has no town list; places are Scandinavian and Icelandic GeoNames places.

nubian-fortified.note: No Nubian style; Egypt and Sudan Arabic.

pnw-plank-village.note: Plateau, Coast and Californian tribes of the Pan-Native-American list; very few Northwest Coast entries.

roman-core.note: Praenomina and cognomina as forenames, gentilicia as surnames; places from the Roman overlay countries.

sahel.note: Hausa and Islamic traditional lists; surnames are frequent Sahelian family names.

siberian-camp.note: No Evenki or Yakut style; Kazakh list and Mongolian names stand in.

slavic-gord.note: Places from the Slavic macro zone.

stilt-town.note: Malaysian pools plus Islamic traditional list.

tibetan-monastery.note: Tibetan names; places are Nepali GeoNames places.

yoruba.note: Traditional Yoruba names; surnames add frequent Yoruba-region surnames.

inheritance_rules.given_only: no family part on the person; the pool surnames still name houses and families
inheritance_rules.matrilineal: same, walking through the mother first
inheritance_rules.order: `family_first` prints the family part before the forename
inheritance_rules.patrilineal: family name drawn from the pool for the oldest known ancestor through the father (else the mother)
inheritance_rules.patronymic: family part built from the father's forename with `form` (male/female templates, `{f}` = forename; `stem_rules` = [ending, replacement, male suffix, female suffix], first match wins); a founder's father is a keyed draw from the male forenames; the pool surnames still name houses

limitations: Frequencies and places are present-day; period lists are generator lists, not attested censuses; some fantasy styles ignore gender; patronymic stems are approximate; see each culture's fit, period and note.

period_bases.fantasy: Namebench fantasy generators: no real-world period
period_bases.modern-unranked: present-day names with no frequency rank: no period signal
period_bases.period-list: Namebench historical-era generator lists, read directly (strongest period signal)
period_bases.ranked-core: frequent present-day names only (rank cut, clean spelling)
period_bases.ranked-core+lexicon: frequent present-day names that also occur in a historical-era list
period_bases.traditional-list: Namebench ethnic generator lists of traditional names (undated)

real.biblicals.era: Biblical names, used by medieval Christians, Jews and Muslims

period_note: Namebench has no dated name frequencies. Each culture declares, per pool, the basis of its names (see `period` in each culture: the dominant basis of the forenames, and the count of each basis per pool; `period_summary` lists the dominant basis). Setting: medieval and fantasy, c. 500-1600.

provenance.derived: values read from Namebench's historical, ethnic or fantasy list generators
provenance.imported: values sampled from Namebench's real-name and GeoNames tables (present-day data)

selection: SHA-256 keyed sample of the union of a pool's sources; real names are the most frequent ones (rank cut 700 for forenames, 3000 for surnames), unranked names only when too few ranked ones exist; places are GeoNames PPL of 1,000-30,000 inhabitants (widened to any populated place when fewer than the target); trailing '(gloss)' removed; NFC; letters, spaces, hyphens and apostrophes only; deduplicated; sorted by code point.
